page.layout: One page of text in a single column of verse, with two numbered poem titles (16 and 17) set as headings. Running head at top, page number at top left. A stray edge of the neighbouring page at the far right is not transcribed.

p.i: Quemcunque Mundi cæcus amor rapit Illum cupido torquet inefficax, Si dentur ingentes auaro Diuitiæ sitit ampliores: Et qui cupitis gaudet honoribus Maioris optat præmia gloriæ: Si non iuuabit res parata Sufficiens aliena poscet. Nil est habenti cuncta cupidine Cui semper ardet pectus auarius, Quémq; orbe terret subiugato Pauperies miseranda semper.

Quem cura tristis, quem labor improbus Per saxa, & ignes sollicitum rapit: Quem non morantur sæua Brumæ Frigora, nec maris inquieti Fluctus, ut addat gaudia gaudijs, Utque auctioris summa pecuniæ Accrescat, ut votis potitus Vitam agat usque beatiorem: Quem non fatigant pondera grandia: Qui pertinaci diffugientia Mercatur inuidæ quietis Commoda, non sapiens, labore,

page.notes: The poem titles "16." and "17." are numbered items; I treated them as level 2 headings. "sitit" (line 4 of the first poem) and "inuidæ" (line 14 of the second) are read from the scan with the long s taken as s; the printed forms look like "fitit" and "inuifæ", so these two readings are doubtful. "cuncta" is also doubtful: the scan shows a letter with a ligature-like form that may be a printer's variant. The word "tousiours" in the title is set as printed with long s. A stray letter at the far right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is left out.
